answer: Operator-Linked Resource Ledger. Each new identity must draw from a shared, per-operator pool of compute and storage credits tracked across its nebula of addresses, so wallets cannot multiply independently. When one identity is flagged, the pool enters a reef state: all linked identities lose credit drawdown until repayment. This forces the attacker into a spiral of replenishment costs, paying full compute price for every synthetic identity rather than once.
